title: Attestation
description: Evidence for a control that genuinely has no query behind it. A documented manual procedure on a defined cadence is legitimate evidence - evidence-pipeline section 5 says so explicitly - and without a way to express it, every control whose system exposes no API sits withheld forever and the inventory silently narrows to whatever happens to have a REST endpoint. AWS Identity Center publishes no per-user MFA state at all; that is not a gap somebody can close by trying harder. What is NOT legitimate is letting an attestation look like telemetry, so every field here exists to keep the two distinguishable: a named human, a stated basis, a mandatory expiry, and a confidence tier that can never reach the one a query earns.

attested_by.description: A named person. Not a team, not a role, not an alias - an attestation is somebody putting their name to a claim, and 'the security team attests' is nobody attesting. The validator refuses obvious placeholders.

expires_at.description: MANDATORY, and enforced. An attestation without an expiry is a claim that quietly becomes false - the same defect as an exception with no expiry, which this repository already refuses. Past its expiry the control is WITHHELD, never failed: the claim has gone stale, which is not the same as the control having broken.

statement.description: What is being attested, quantified over the population the control defines. Same discipline as a control assertion: 'MFA is enabled' is not a statement, 'every one of the 4 workforce identities has a phishing-resistant factor enrolled' is.

basis.description: HOW the person knows - what they actually looked at, when. This is the field an assessor reads to decide whether to believe the attestation, and it is the one that makes a lazy attestation visibly lazy.

method.description: console-review is somebody reading a screen. vendor-report is a report from the system owner. sampled-inspection is explicitly a sample and caps the tier lower still, because a sample is not a population and this repository does not pretend otherwise.

population_definition.description: Must match the control record's wording. Drift between the two is a finding, exactly as it is for a query_ref - an attestation about a different population than the control defines is not evidence for that control.

failing.description: Enumerated, exactly as a queried assertion must. An attestation claiming failures it cannot name is an opinion; the whole point of the population discipline is that the exceptions are identified so somebody can work them.

why_no_query.description: Why this cannot be a query. Required so an attestation is a considered choice rather than the easy path: 'the vendor exposes no API for it' is a reason, 'we have not built the collector yet' is a backlog item and should not become a permanent attestation.

evidence_ref.description: Pointer to the artifact the attester looked at - a ticket, a report, a document store path. Never the artifact itself: this repository does not become a screenshot locker.
